syllabus_topics: General description of railway system components.
Curve, cant and railway concepts.
Railway signalling and transport capacity concepts.
Wheel-rail adhesion.
Running resistance.
Effect of rotational masses (wheelsets, traction drive).
General description and components of traction system (mechanical, electrical).
Specification of traction drive components (motors, gearboxes) for specific vehicles and operational conditions.
General description and components of braking system (mechanical, pneumatic).
Specification of Braking system components (brake discs, brake cylinders) for specific vehicles and operational conditions.
General description and components of suspension system (mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic).
Concepts of frequency behaviour of the vehicle and comfort.
Specification of suspension components (air springs, dampers) for specific vehicles and operational conditions.
Types and construction of tyres.
Longitudinal Forces (Slip Ratio).
Lateral Forces (Slip Angle).
Combined Forces (Friction Circle).
Autoaligning moment and Rolling Resistance.
Acting forces: traction/braking, aerodynamic force, rolling resistance, load.
Acceleration: Longitudinal load transfer and gear boxes design.
Braking: brake distribution.
Ackermann.
Bicycle model.
Understeering/Oversteering and Yaw gain.
Lateral Load transfer: Influence of roll centre and suspension stiffness.
assessment_rules: It is compulsory to get a minimum score of 50% in each part (Railway and Automobile) to pass the course. For the Automobile part, a minimum score of 50% is required in its final exam to pass that part. In the extraordinary assessment, students only repeat failed parts, and marks from passed parts (including project marks) are maintained. The minimum score requirements remain applicable during the extraordinary assessment.
